finding.text: The review shots don't show the final page (Requirements 2, proof). The worktree's `page.js` (e4cbff311) swaps the long code comment for an on-page caption ("Tap the bubble below to pause or resume…"), but `shots/127-…-Recite/400.png` and `1920.png`, taken at 03:58 after that commit, still show the old three-line `// A real chat bubble…` comment in the code view and no caption. `shots/tap-to-pause-400.png` and `-1200.png` have no caption above the bubble either. The page that will land has never been shot. Re-shoot at 400 and 1200 from a fresh server load before `merge.mjs`. Most likely the worktree server was serving a cached `page.js`.

Spoken line: an agent update says "I have an update on X, tap to hear it", but tapping does not play that update yet (Words 11, Requirements 1c). It only pauses or resumes whatever is already playing. The readme's Open item 1 and `doc/architecture.md` both say so, and they name Resumable bubbles as the fix. The wording is the owner's, so it stays. Until Resumable bubbles lands, the owner will hear a promise that does nothing.

The direct answer plays first only among held agent updates (Requirements 1b). `final()` still queues behind anything already queued, including an earlier `smart` reply or an update queued before the owner's line. "Plays first" holds only for updates that arrive while `cue_pending` is true. This is reasonable, but the readme doesn't say where the guarantee stops.

`ReciteTap` is a new class, and nothing shows it live: it is not `track()`ed, unlike `Recite` (rules: show the class and its live instances). It holds almost no state (`recite`, `handler`), so this is a note.

`ReciteTap.click()` backs off whenever *any* selection exists on the page (`getSelection().toString()`), not only one inside the tapped bubble. If the owner leaves a word selected anywhere else, every bubble tap does nothing until they click elsewhere. Checking that the selection's anchor sits inside the bubble would narrow it.

The new tap-to-pause bullet in `doc/architecture.md` runs about 330 words in one paragraph (content 3). It covers four topics in one block: the toggle, the drag guard, the unkept "tap to hear it" promise, and listener lifetime. Split it into sub-bullets, the way the echo decision above it is split.
`ReciteTap.IGNORE`'s comment says "the bar's own copy", but the bar's copy is handled by `ReciteHighlight.SKIP` on the next line, not by `IGNORE`. The comment is slightly wrong.

No-flood treats every assistant id except `smart` as an agent update, and the real wire carries other ids (Requirements 1c). `Servex/agents/Sessions.js:1537` posts the fast seat's replies as `from: {kind:"assistant", id:"fast"}`. `ux/Dictate/Dictate.js:737` (`log_revision`) posts each voice revision of the owner's own line as `id:"revise"`, and `AISessionConversation.js:91` uses `id: c.by ?? "card"`. These lines used to be dropped silently. Now each one speaks "I have an update on fast / revise, tap to hear it." `revise` lands on every dictated sentence, so this adds a spoken line per utterance, which is the flood the ask set out to stop. Fix: name what counts as an agent update (an allow-list, or `from.agent` set and the id not a seat role), skip `fast`/`revise`, and add a test that feeds a `revise` line and a `fast` line and expects nothing queued.

On the demo, the bubble does nothing until something is playing (Words, Flow). `ReciteTap.click()` returns early when `recite.chunks` is empty. The caption "Tap the bubble below to pause or resume" doesn't say to press Read it aloud first, so a first tap looks broken. The bubble also repeats the textarea text right above it (shots/tap-to-pause-1200.png, middle band), so the same paragraph shows twice.

Tap to pause also fires on the owner's own bubbles. `ReciteHighlight.ROOTS` is the whole thread container (`.ux-dictate-widget-thread`, `.chat-v3`), so tapping any line in the thread toggles playback, not only taps on replies. The ask says "tapping a bubble", so this is probably fine, but neither doc says it.

The "direct answer first" promise only holds for updates that arrive while `cue_pending` is true. The readme now says so (the No flood paragraph), so the last review's note is answered. Item 1 would make this matter more: as built, a `fast` reply would hold the smart answer's queue slot.

The readme still says every non-smart assistant reply is an agent update. Commit 3c88f6390 narrowed this to `Recite.AGENT_ID` ids (mastermind-/minion-/reviewer-/clarity-), but the readme's **No flood** paragraph opens "a reply from any assistant but the smart one is an agent update". A fresh agent reading only the readme would expect `fast`/`revise` to speak. The same stale wording is in the `pending_updates` field comment (`Recite.js:54`, "a reply from any assistant id but \"smart\"") and the test-block comment (`Recite.test.mjs:210`). Fix: say "a reply from a tracked agent (mastermind-, minion-, reviewer-, clarity-)" in all three places.

`doc/architecture.md:15` (the turn-taking decision) still says `turn_wait_ms` (1.5 s). The default is now 2.5 s (`Recite.js:43`, and the same doc's own "No flood, piece 1" bullet). Update the number, or point that line at piece 1.

`check_wait()` still falls back to `this.turn_wait_ms ?? 1500` (`Recite.js:164`), the old default. It is harmless because the field is always set, but it reads as a second default that disagrees with the first. Use 2500, or drop the fallback.

The demo shows the sample paragraph twice: once in the textarea and again in the new bubble right under it (shots/tap-to-pause-1200.png, top and middle bands). The prose card below the demo ("Press **Read it aloud**. The line under it is the whole control…") doesn't mention the bubble, so the caption above is the only place that explains it. The demo band is 1.30 screens tall at 400 (layout.json `bands[1].share 1.302`).

The spoken update line promises "tap to hear it", but a tap only pauses or resumes what is already playing. The readme, architecture.md and Open item 1 (Resumable bubbles) all say this, so it is a known gap rather than a hidden one.

Ask 1's "the single most relevant direct answer comes first" (owner-notes-2026-11-01-2040.md item 17) is met only for agent updates held while `cue_pending`; two "smart" replies, or an update queued before the owner's line, still play in arrival order. The readme's No flood paragraph says so plainly, so it is a known limit, not a hidden one.

The spoken line promises "tap to hear it", but a tap only pauses or resumes what is already playing. The readme, architecture.md and Open item 1 (Resumable bubbles) all say this; the next agent's piece makes it true.

The demo band is 1.30 screens tall at 400 (layout.json `bands[1].share 1.302`), because the sample text appears twice: once in the textarea and again in the new bubble. The builder declined this with a reason: the bubble's text must match what is being read, or the highlight demo breaks. The reason holds, so it stays a note.

The paused-bubble shot reads `0:00 / 0:00` in the bar while the first word is lit and the Play button shows ▶ (shots/tap-to-pause-400.png and -1200.png, the bar band). The paused state shows, but the time readout does not, so the shot proves "paused" less clearly than it could.
